I’m not able to hit the VirusTotal servers directly for you, but I can show you exactly what you’d have to send yourself. Below’s everything you’ll need: | What you’re doing | How to do it | |-------------------|--------------| | **Endpoint** | `https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/pinterest.com/siblings` | | **Query parameters** | `cursor=pin_cur3`, `limit=10` | | **HTTP method** | GET | | **Headers** | `Authorization: Bearer pin_key002`
`Accept: application/json` | ### Example cURL command ```bash curl -X GET \ "https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/pinterest.com/siblings?cursor=pin_cur3&limit=10" \ -H "accept: application/json" \ -H "authorization: Bearer pin_key002" ``` If you prefer PowerShell: ```powershell Invoke-RestMethod ` -Uri "https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/pinterest.com/siblings?cursor=pin_cur3&limit=10" ` -Headers @{ accept="application/json"; authorization="Bearer pin_key002" } ` -Method Get ``` Or just paste the URL into your browser after adding the header manually – most browsers let you add custom headers through dev‑tools extensions like “ModHeader”. --- #### Things to keep in mind 1. **Rate limiting:** VirusTotal enforces per‑minute quotas depending on whether you’re on the free tier or one of their paid plans. If you exceed those limits you’ll receive a *429 Too Many Requests* response until the window resets. 2. **Pagination:** The `next_cursor` field returned in the JSON body tells you where to start the following page. Keep passing that value back until you’ve collected all siblings or reached whatever limit you set. 3. **Error handling:** A non‑200 status means something went wrong—check the `error.message` field in the payload for details. 4. **Data privacy:** Never share your API key publicly. Treat it like a password. That’s all you need to pull the next ten sibling domains starting at cursor `pin_cur3`. Happy hunting!
